newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Finland's Rehn withdraws from U.N. rights post race.
newsitem.headline: Finland's Rehn withdraws from U.N. rights post race.

text.p: Finland's former defence minister, ELizabeth Rehn, said on Tuesday she had withdrawn her candidacy for the U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights, leaving Ireland's President Mary Robinson as the main candidate for the post.

Rehn, who was not considered a front-runner, said in a statement she had "chosen not to run for the office" and instead would complete her current mission in Yugoslavia where she is a U.N. human rights investigator and now is also responsible for tracing missing persons in the Balkans.

"The time is now criticial for the implementation of the civilian part of the (Balkan) peace agreement," the statement said, adding that she had told U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan of her decision.

Robinson's candidacy received a boost last Thursday when Sonia Picado, Costa Rica's ambassdor to Washington, and a leading contender, said Annan had not offered her the job. It was her second meeting with the secretary-general.
Annan is not expected to announce his decision until July.

Robinson, also a lawyer and human rights expert, does not end her seven-year term as president of Ireland until December although there are reports she would be available in November. She is backed by the United States and Britain while Picado was supported by Third World countries.

The position, first proposed nearly 50 years ago, became vacant after Jose Ayala Lasso resigned in March as the first U.N. human rights commissioner to become Ecuador's foreign minister. He was appointed in 1994 for four years.
In the interim, the job is being carried out by Briton Ralph Zacklin, a deputy to the U.N. under-secretary general for legal affairs.
